views.name: match_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  m.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal
FROM Match m
WHERE m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
  AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one row per Match with confirmed (non-null) home and away goals, useful for scoring, result, and per-match analyses.
params.when_to_use: When you need match-level scores (home and away goals) for aggregation or result determination. | To compute match outcomes (win/draw/loss) or goal-based metrics per match and then aggregate to teams, leagues, or seasons. | As a safe, granular source when composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total goals per season) after appropriate aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the match (derived from Match.id) | league_id: identifier of the league the match belongs to (derived from Match.league_id) | season: season identifier for the match (derived from Match.season) | home_team_goal: integer number of goals scored by the home team in this match (derived from Match.home_team_goal) | away_team_goal: integer number of goals scored by the away team in this match (derived from Match.away_team_goal)
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal
params.metric: home_team_goal = identity(Match.home_team_goal)  -- a per-row (match) measure; not an aggregate | away_team_goal = identity(Match.away_team_goal)  -- a per-row (match) measure; not an aggregate | total_goals_per_match = (home_team_goal + away_team_goal)  -- can be computed per-row from the two grounded columns; aggregation (SUM) required to get totals across multiple matches
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a league dimension or seasons dimension on league_id or season (e.g., JOIN league_dim ON match_row_level.league_id = league_dim.id) — safe because match_row_level is one row per Match.id and these are one-to-many (dimension-to-fact) relationships that will not duplicate match-level measures when enriching with dimension attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a teams dimension on team id (if joining either home or away team attributes) using the team id from the Match table (not included in this view). To avoid duplication, join each team separately (e.g., home_team_dim on Match.home_team_id) and do not join multiple one-to-many event tables without aggregation. | do NOT join to another one-to-many fact table (e.g., events, goals_by_minute, substitutions) on match_id directly without first aggregating that other table to match_id level, because joining a one-to-many table will multiply match_row_level rows and thus multiply its per-match measures (home_team_goal, away_team_goal). If you must combine with a one-to-many table, aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per match (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY match_id) before joining. | when aggregating this view: treat home_team_goal and away_team_goal as per-match base measures. To get totals across a grouping (season, league, team), use SUM(home_team_goal) and SUM(away_team_goal) or SUM(home_team_goal + away_team_goal) after grouping. If computing team-level metrics, ensure each match contributes to the correct team side (home vs away) or pivot/normalize rows to team-match grain before summing to avoid double counting. | joining multiple match-level rows: this view is at grain match.id (one row per match). Joins that preserve match.id uniqueness (one-to-one or many-to-one from dimensions) are safe; joins that introduce multiple rows per match require re-aggregation of measures from this view or pre-aggregation of the other side.

views.description: Provides one row per Match with confirmed (non-null) home and away goals, useful for scoring, result, and per-match analyses.

views.name: match_goals_per_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  (COALESCE(m.home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(m.away_team_goal,0)) AS total_goals
FROM match_row_level m

params.description: Provides total goals scored in each match (match-level total = home_team_goal + away_team_goal) for matches in the match_row_level table.
params.when_to_use: Ask: What was the total number of goals in a specific match (by match id)? | Aggregate: Compose match-level total_goals into season- or league-level totals/averages by aggregating this view (e.g., total goals per season, average goals per match in a league). | Filter & compare: Compare or filter matches by total_goals (e.g., find matches with more than N goals). | Join-safe enrichment: Enrich matches with attributes from one-row-per-match or one-row-per-league dimension tables without duplicating the match-level total_goals.
params.output_schema: id: unique match identifier — derived from base column match_row_level.id | league_id: identifier of the league the match belongs to — derived from base column match_row_level.league_id | season: season identifier/value for the match — derived from base column match_row_level.season | total_goals: match-level metric equal to home_team_goal + away_team_goal (nulls treated as 0) — derived from match_row_level.home_team_goal and match_row_level.away_team_goal
params.grounded_columns: match_row_level.id | match_row_level.league_id | match_row_level.season | match_row_level.home_team_goal | match_row_level.away_team_goal
params.metric: total_goals = COALESCE(match_row_level.home_team_goal, 0) + COALESCE(match_row_level.away_team_goal, 0)  -- match-level derived expression (not an aggregate)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any one-row-per-league or one-row-per-season dimension (e.g., league or season dimension) on league_id or season — safe because match_goals_per_match is one-row-per-match (id) so joining to a single-row-per-league/season dimension does not duplicate match rows or change total_goals. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match-level tables or views keyed by match_row_level.id (or this view's id) — safe because it's a one-to-one or one-row-per-match relationship, so total_goals remains stable. | unsafe joins (must re-aggregate first): do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child table or view (for example: events, player_actions, tickets, or any table having multiple rows per match) without aggregating that child to match-level first — such joins will multiply match_goals_per_match rows and therefore duplicate total_goals. Instead, aggregate the child to match_id (e.g., COUNT(*) AS events_per_match) and then join on id. | unsafe joins (must re-aggregate first): do NOT join to tables that are many-to-many to matches (e.g., match-player assignments with multiple players per match) unless those tables are pre-aggregated to one row per match, because otherwise measures from this view would be multiplied. | composition pattern for roll-up: to compute league-level sum of goals, GROUP BY league_id (and optionally season) on this view and SUM(total_goals). This preserves correctness because total_goals is match-level and grouping by league/season aggregates matches without duplication.

views.description: Provides total goals scored in each match (match-level total = home_team_goal + away_team_goal) for matches in the match_row_level table.

views.name: league_match_aggregate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  COUNT(m.id) AS match_count,
  SUM(m.home_team_goal + m.away_team_goal) AS total_goals
FROM match_row_level AS m
WHERE m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
  AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  m.league_id,
  m.season

params.description: Aggregated per-league per-season match counts and total goals (sums of home+away goals) for matches with non-null goal values.
params.when_to_use: Get number of matches and total goals for each league in a given season (or across seasons). | Compute averages or rates per league-season when you can divide/merge these aggregates (e.g., goals per match = total_goals / match_count). | Join league-level or season-level dimensional attributes (league name, country, season metadata) without changing aggregates. | Build higher-level summaries (e.g., per-league across seasons) by re-aggregating these rows.
params.output_schema: league_id: identifier for the league (derived from match_row_level.league_id) | season: season identifier (derived from match_row_level.season) | match_count: count of matches for that league+season where both home_team_goal and away_team_goal are NOT NULL (derived from COUNT(match_row_level.id)) | total_goals: sum of goals scored in those matches, computed as SUM(home_team_goal + away_team_goal) from match_row_level
params.grounded_columns: match_row_level.league_id | match_row_level.season | match_row_level.id | match_row_level.home_team_goal | match_row_level.away_team_goal
params.metric: match_count = COUNT(match_row_level.id) -- cardinality measure: counts qualifying match rows per (league_id, season) | total_goals = SUM(match_row_level.home_team_goal + match_row_level.away_team_goal) -- additive metric: total goals summed over qualifying match rows per (league_id, season)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-league dimension (e.g., league table/view keyed by league_id) on league_id — safe because league_match_aggregate is one-row-per (league_id, season) and joining a league dimension (one row per league_id) will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-season dimension (e.g., season table/view keyed by season) on season — safe because season dimension is one row per season and will not duplicate measures. | re-aggregation guidance: when composing across seasons or leagues (for example, to get totals per league across multiple seasons), aggregate the rows of this view (e.g., SUM(total_goals), SUM(match_count)) rather than joining to a one-to-many detail table. | avoid joining without re-aggregation: do NOT join this view to any one-to-many detail table or view (for example, match_row_level again, or any events/plays table keyed to match id) without first re-aggregating or ensuring uniqueness, because such joins will duplicate match_count and total_goals (they are aggregated at league_id+season and would be multiplied by the number of matching detail rows). | avoid joining to sibling one-to-many views: do NOT join directly to match_row_level or other match-detail views (one row per match or per event) on league_id and season, unless you GROUP BY league_id, season after the join to re-aggregate the measures to the intended grain. | safe composition with normalized sibling: You may join with match_goals_per_match (if that view is one-row-per-match) only by matching on (match_id) after un-aggregating or by re-aggregating appropriately; joining match_goals_per_match to this aggregated view on league_id+season without re-aggregation is unsafe because match_goals_per_match is likely one-to-one with matches and would multiply aggregate rows.

views.description: Aggregated per-league per-season match counts and total goals (sums of home+away goals) for matches with non-null goal values.

views.name: matches_in_league_season_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_api_id,
  league_id,
  season,
  date,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal
FROM
  "Match"
WHERE
  match_api_id IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one row per match with its league, season, date, teams, and final score — useful for match-level reporting and as a stable row-level match cohort to build further aggregations.
params.when_to_use: List or filter matches in a given league and season | Compute match-level results, e.g. winner/loser/draw, goal difference per match | Join match metadata to team-, player-, or event-level data when you need a single row per match as the driving rowset | Seed higher-level aggregations (per-team-per-season, per-league-per-season) by aggregating this match-level view
params.output_schema: match_api_id: unique match identifier; derived directly from Match.match_api_id | league_id: league identifier the match belongs to; derived directly from Match.league_id | season: season label for the match (e.g., '2011/2012'); derived directly from Match.season | date: match date (as stored in Match.date); derived directly from Match.date | home_team_api_id: home team identifier for the match; derived directly from Match.home_team_api_id | away_team_api_id: away team identifier for the match; derived directly from Match.away_team_api_id | home_team_goal: integer goals scored by the home team in this match; derived directly from Match.home_team_goal | away_team_goal: integer goals scored by the away team in this match; derived directly from Match.away_team_goal
params.grounded_columns: Match.match_api_id | Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.date | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal
params.metric: home_team_goal = Match.home_team_goal | away_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal | match_count = COUNT(match_api_id) -- when aggregated over this view, count of matches | goals_for_home = SUM(home_team_goal) -- when aggregated grouped by a dimension (e.g., home_team_api_id) | goals_for_away = SUM(away_team_goal) -- when aggregated grouped by a dimension (e.g., away_team_api_id) | total_goals_per_match = (home_team_goal + away_team_goal) -- row-level expression; can be SUM(total_goals_per_match) after aggregation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team dimension views/tables on team id (e.g., team.id = home_team_api_id or team.id = away_team_api_id) — safe because this view has exactly one row per match_api_id and joining to a team dimension (one row per team) will not duplicate match rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league or season dimension tables on league_id or season — safe because those are one-row-per-league/per-season dimensions and will not multiply this view's rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/detail tables (e.g., match events, player appearances, or any row-level table that contains multiple rows per match) without re-aggregation on the many side first — such joins will duplicate match rows and thus multiply match-level measures like home_team_goal/away_team_goal. Instead: aggregate the many-side to match_api_id (e.g., SUM or COUNT grouped by match_api_id) and then join the aggregated result to this view on match_api_id. | when composing team-season aggregates: avoid joining this view twice (once for home and once for away) without appropriate grouping/aggregation. For example, to compute goals per team per season, UNION/UNPIVOT home and away contributions or aggregate with grouped SUMs over CASE expressions to prevent double counting. | safe to join to sibling aggregated views that are explicitly at match_api_id grain (e.g., match_goals_per_match) because they share the same 1:1 match_api_id cardinality; avoid joining to any sibling aggregate at a coarser grain without aggregating this view up to that coarser grain first. | note on uniqueness: this view filters out rows with NULL match_api_id, so match_api_id can be treated as the row key for composition and as the identifier guaranteeing one row per match in downstream planners.

views.description: Provides one row per match with its league, season, date, teams, and final score — useful for match-level reporting and as a stable row-level match cohort to build further aggregations.

views.name: team_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  team_api_id,
  team_long_name,
  team_short_name,
  id
FROM Team

params.description: Provides one-row-per-team identifiers and canonical team names for joining or reporting about teams.
params.when_to_use: Look up team names or canonical IDs when building reports about teams | Join team descriptive attributes (long/short name) onto match- or league-level aggregates | Compose downstream SQL that needs a stable team key (team_api_id) and human-readable names
params.output_schema: team_api_id: external/team API identifier for the team — derived directly from Team.team_api_id | team_long_name: full/human-readable team name — derived directly from Team.team_long_name | team_short_name: short/abbreviated team name — derived directly from Team.team_short_name | id: internal surrogate key for the team row in the Team table — derived directly from Team.id
params.grounded_columns: Team.team_api_id | Team.team_long_name | Team.team_short_name | Team.id
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated metrics. All output columns are direct column projections: team_api_id = Team.team_api_id, team_long_name = Team.team_long_name, team_short_name = Team.team_short_name, id = Team.id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match-level or aggregate views on team_api_id (or Team.id) — safe because team_identity is one-row-per-team (grain = team_api_id) so joining it onto many-row match or goal tables will not duplicate team_identity rows, and its descriptive columns are dimension-like. | Join to match_row_level (SEL) on match_row_level.home_team_api_id = team_identity.team_api_id or match_row_level.away_team_api_id = team_identity.team_api_id — safe because team_identity has a single row per team, the match rows remain the many side and team columns are not aggregated here. | Join to match_goals_per_match (NORM) or league_match_aggregate (AGG) on the appropriate team key to add team names to those aggregates — safe only when those aggregates are already properly aggregated per team or per match as intended. Since team_identity contains no measures, it will not duplicate measures, but ensure you do not accidentally join team_identity in a way that multiplies rows and then sum duplicated aggregates without re-aggregation. | Do NOT join team_identity to one-to-many child tables (e.g., players, events) expecting those child-table measures to remain at team granularity without re-aggregation. If you join to a one-to-many table and then aggregate, you must re-aggregate (e.g., use GROUP BY team_api_id) to avoid multiplying measures. | When composing with sibling selection views like matches_in_league_season_cohort(SEL), join on team_api_id only to bring in names; if you need aggregated metrics by team after joining to many-row sources, compute aggregates after the join or join to an aggregate view (e.g., league_match_aggregate) instead.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-team identifiers and canonical team names for joining or reporting about teams.

views.name: away_match_results
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  M.match_api_id AS match_api_id,
  M.away_team_api_id AS away_team_api_id,
  M.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal,
  M.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  CASE
    WHEN M.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
     AND M.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
     AND M.away_team_goal > M.home_team_goal THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_away_win
FROM
  "Match" AS M

params.description: One-row-per-match facts for away-team results: away team id, goals scored/conceded, and whether the away team won.
params.when_to_use: Get the away-side outcome for individual matches (did the away team win?). | Build per-team or per-season aggregates about away performance by aggregating this view. | Filter or join match-level analyses where only away-team perspective is needed (e.g., away wins, away goals). | Compose with lineups, events, or team identity to analyze away performance by team or cohort — provided joins preserve one-row-per-match or you re-aggregate after many-to-one joins.
params.output_schema: match_api_id: unique match identifier (from Match.match_api_id). Grain: one row per match_api_id. | away_team_api_id: away team identifier for the match (from Match.away_team_api_id). | away_team_goal: number of goals scored by the away team in that match (from Match.away_team_goal). | home_team_goal: number of goals scored by the home team in that match (from Match.home_team_goal). | is_away_win: boolean/int flag (1 or 0). Computed as 1 when away_team_goal and home_team_goal are both NOT NULL and away_team_goal > home_team_goal, else 0. (derived expression in the view)
params.grounded_columns: Match.match_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.away_team_goal | Match.home_team_goal
params.metric: is_away_win = CASE WHEN Match.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND Match.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND Match.away_team_goal > Match.home_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | away_team_goal (per-row measure) = Match.away_team_goal | home_team_goal (per-row measure) = Match.home_team_goal
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_identity on away_team_api_id (JOIN team_identity ON away_team_api_id = team_identity.team_api_id) — safe because away_match_results is one-row-per-match and team_identity is one-row-per-team, so measures remain one per match. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_in_league_season_cohort on match_api_id (JOIN matches_in_league_season_cohort ON match_api_id = matches_in_league_season_cohort.match_api_id) — safe because matches_in_league_season_cohort is a selector of matches (one-row-per-match) and will not duplicate rows. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables (for example, joining to a match events table or player appearances without aggregation) because those will duplicate this view's per-match rows and over-count measures like away_team_goal and is_away_win. If you must combine with one-to-many data, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side to match_api_id first (e.g., SUM(events.x) GROUP BY match_api_id) and then join on match_api_id, or | - join and then re-aggregate by match_api_id to restore one-row-per-match before computing metrics derived from away_match_results. | safe composition with aggregations: you may aggregate this view to team or season level (e.g., SUM(is_away_win) GROUP BY away_team_api_id) to compute counts of away wins per team — this is the intended pattern for building higher-level metrics. | joins listed as safe do NOT duplicate measures because they are many-to-one (away_match_results -> team_identity) or one-to-one (selector views keyed by match_api_id). Any join to a multi-row-per-match source requires re-aggregation to avoid multiplicative duplication.

views.description: One-row-per-match facts for away-team results: away team id, goals scored/conceded, and whether the away team won.

views.name: team_attributes_non_null_build_up_play_speed

SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass
FROM Team_Attributes
WHERE buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT NULL

params.description: Rows of Team_Attributes where buildUpPlaySpeed is present — supplies each team's buildUpPlaySpeed value and its categorical class on the Team_Attributes row level.
params.when_to_use: Look up a team's buildUpPlaySpeed value and class on the Team_Attributes row identified by id. | Filter or join to Team_Attributes rows that have a non-null buildUpPlaySpeed before computing aggregates (e.g., team-season averages) so aggregation only uses measured rows. | Serve as a safe base (one-row-per-id) to compose higher-level aggregates (team-season, team-history) when joined/aggregated correctly.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier of the Team_Attributes row (Team_Attributes.id) | team_api_id: foreign team identifier (Team_Attributes.team_api_id) | team_fifa_api_id: alternate team identifier (Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id) | date: date for this Team_Attributes observation (Team_Attributes.date) | buildUpPlaySpeed: numeric measured metric for buildUpPlaySpeed (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed) — raw value from the source row | buildUpPlaySpeedClass: categorical class associated with buildUpPlaySpeed (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass) — raw class label from the source row
params.grounded_columns: Team_Attributes.id | Team_Attributes.team_api_id | Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id | Team_Attributes.date | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass
params.metric: buildUpPlaySpeed = Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed (row-level raw numeric value, not an aggregate) | buildUpPlaySpeedClass = Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass (row-level categorical label)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_identity (NORM) on team_identity.team_api_id = team_attributes_non_null_build_up_play_speed.team_api_id — safe because team_identity is one-row-per-team (dimension) so it will not duplicate this view's rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_in_league_season_cohort (SEL) only when joining on a key that is one-to-one with Team_Attributes.id (there is no such key here); do NOT join directly on team_api_id to matches_in_league_season_cohort without aggregating matches first, because matches are one-to-many per team and would duplicate buildUpPlaySpeed rows. | do NOT join to match_row_level (SEL) or away_match_results (JOIN) on team_api_id or team identifiers without first aggregating match_row_level/away_match_results to the same grain (Team_Attributes.id or team_api_id + date bucket). match_row_level and away_match_results are one-to-many relative to Team_Attributes and will multiply buildUpPlaySpeed if joined directly. | when composing team-season metrics (for example: average buildUpPlaySpeed per team-season), aggregate this view at the desired season/team keys (e.g., AVG(buildUpPlaySpeed) GROUP BY team_api_id, season) before joining to season- or match-level tables to avoid duplication. | when joining to league_match_aggregate (AGG) or match_goals_per_match (NORM), ensure both sides are aggregated to compatible grains (e.g., team-season) because those views may be aggregated differently; only join when the join keys represent a single row on the other side or after re-aggregation to a single row to preserve correct metrics. | in short: safe to join to one-row-per-team or one-row-per-Team_Attributes.id dimensions on matching keys; avoid or re-aggregate before joining to any table/view that is known to be one-to-many (matches, match events, or other row-level match tables) so measures from this view are not multiplied.

views.name: team_max_build_up_play_speed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ta.id AS id,
  ta.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  MAX(ta.buildUpPlaySpeed) AS max_buildUpPlaySpeed
FROM Team_Attributes ta
WHERE ta.buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ta.team_api_id

params.description: Per-team maximum observed buildUpPlaySpeed from Team_Attributes rows (one row per team_api_id).
params.when_to_use: Find the highest buildUpPlaySpeed value recorded for each team across all Team_Attributes rows. | Compare teams by their maximum historical buildUpPlaySpeed. | Compose team-level features that need a single representative (max) buildUpPlaySpeed per team before joining to match- or event-level data. | Filter or rank teams by their peak buildUpPlaySpeed in downstream analyses.
params.output_schema: team_api_id: Team identifier (derived from Team_Attributes.team_api_id). This is the grouping key (grain of the view). | max_buildUpPlaySpeed: Maximum buildUpPlaySpeed observed for the team (derived from MAX(Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed)).
params.grounded_columns: Team_Attributes.id | Team_Attributes.team_api_id | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed
params.metric: max_buildUpPlaySpeed = MAX(Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed) -- aggregate computed over all Team_Attributes rows for a given team_api_id, excluding NULLs as per the WHERE clause
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_identity (or any other team-level one-row-per-team view) on team_api_id — safe because team_max_build_up_play_speed is one row per team_api_id, so its max_buildUpPlaySpeed will not be duplicated when joined to another one-row-per-team relation. | Do NOT directly join this view to match-level or other one-to-many-from-team tables/views (for example, Match or matches_in_league_season_cohort) without re-aggregation or careful handling — such joins will duplicate the max_buildUpPlaySpeed value across multiple match rows and thus multiply its contribution if you then aggregate measures that include it. | If you need team_max_build_up_play_speed available at match granularity, join on team_api_id and then: (a) treat max_buildUpPlaySpeed as a static team attribute (do not SUM it across matches), or (b) re-aggregate after the join in a way that preserves intended semantics (e.g., take AVG or MAX over matches as appropriate). | Safe composition examples: (1) join to team_identity on team_api_id to assemble a team profile with one row per team; (2) left join to a team-level cohort table that is one row per team. Unsafe composition examples: joining to match_goals_per_match, match_row_level, away_match_results, or matches_in_league_season_cohort (all of which are match- or row-level and can have many rows per team) without re-aggregation.

views.description: Per-team maximum observed buildUpPlaySpeed from Team_Attributes rows (one row per team_api_id).

views.name: team_with_name_and_max_build_up_play_speed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  t.team_long_name AS team_long_name,

params.when_to_use: Find each team's maximum buildUpPlaySpeed across Team_Attributes records (e.g., for comparisons or ranking). | Compose team-level analyses that need a single representative buildUpPlaySpeed metric per team (e.g., join to team metadata, season/league aggregations after safe joins). | Filter or join teams by their maximum buildUpPlaySpeed when building dashboards or further SQL that expects one row per team.

This view itself is one-row-per-match so its measures are not duplicated when joining to one-row-per-team dimensions. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_in_league_season_cohort on (league_id, season, id) — safe because matches_in_league_season_cohort is a selector of match rows; joining on the match id preserves one-row-per-match cardinality. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_match_aggregate only when joining on (league_id, season) and treating league_match_aggregate as aggregated per (league_id, season). params.description: Counts of matches and count of drawn matches, aggregated at the league × season grain.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of matches and number of draws for each league in each season | Compute draw rates by league and season (draw_count / match_count) when composing further | Join league-season level metrics into league- or season-level dashboards without re-aggregating match-level data | Filter or compare leagues/seasons by match volume or frequency of draws before joining to other aggregated data

params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal
params.metric: match_count = COUNT(Match.id)  -- count of match rows grouped by Match.league_id, Match.season | draw_count = SUM(CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of matches that ended in a draw
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league-level dimension tables (for example a league dimension keyed by league_id) on league_id — safe because this view has at most one row per (league_id, season) so joining enriches without duplicating these aggregated measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season-level dimension tables on season — safe for the same reason (one row per league_id×season). | do NOT join directly to match_row_level (Match) or any other one-to-many match-level table (e.g., match_row_level, match_row_level_9) on league_id and/or season without re-aggregating the match-level table to league×season first — doing so will multiply rows and thus over-count match_count and draw_count. | do NOT join to team-level one-to-many tables (e.g., multiple teams per league) such as team_identity or team_attributes_non_null_build_up_play_speed on league_id without first aggregating teams to league×season (or otherwise ensuring a one-row-per-league×season join key) because those joins will duplicate this view's measures. | safe composition pattern: if you need to combine with another aggregated view that is not at the same grain, aggregate that view to (league_id, season) first and then join on (league_id, season) — this preserves correctness and avoids double-counting. | example safe join: league_match_draws_per_match JOIN league_dimension ON league_match_draws_per_match.league_id = league_dimension.id  — safe because join is 1:1 or many-dim-to-one-agg, not 1-agg-to-many-dim. | example unsafe join: league_match_draws_per_match JOIN Match ON league_match_draws_per_match.league_id = Match.league_id AND league_match_draws_per_match.season = Match.season  — unsafe because Match is many-per-(league,season) and will multiply match_count and draw_count unless Match is pre-aggregated to the same grain.

However, note player_api_id may appear many times in this view (multiple snapshots), so joining to a one-row-per-player dimension will not duplicate measures per snapshot. | Do NOT blindly join this view to a match-level or other one-to-many table on player_api_id without considering multiplicity — e.g., joining to a matches table that lists multiple matches per player will multiply attribute-row-level snapshots by matches. Each join is one-to-one (team identity is one-row-per-team) and will not duplicate match rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_goals_per_match on Match.id = match_goals_per_match.id — safe because match_goals_per_match is an aggregation at match grain (one row per match) and will not duplicate measures when combined. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_match_aggregate or league_match_draws_per_match on league/season keys only if those sibling views are aggregated at league-season (or match) grain consistent with this view; joining an aggregate that is one-row-per-league-season to this one-row-per-match view is safe only when the aggregate's key (e.g., league_id + season) is used, since it will replicate the aggregate per match but not multiply original match-level measures incorrectly. | do NOT join without care to any one-to-many detail table (for example, event-level or player-level tables) directly to this view if you intend to preserve match-level metrics: joining a match-row to a table with multiple rows per match will multiply match rows and duplicate any match-level measures. views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ta.team_api_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ta.date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  ta.id,
  ta.date,
  ta.buildUpPlayPassing
FROM Team_Attributes ta
JOIN (
  SELECT
    team_api_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    MAX(date) AS max_date
  FROM Team_Attributes
  GROUP BY team_api_id, CAST(strftime('%Y', date) AS INTEGER)
) most_recent
  ON ta.team_api_id = most_recent.team_api_id
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', ta.date) AS INTEGER) = most_recent.year

SELECT
  pa.player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id,
  AVG(pa.heading_accuracy) AS avg_heading_accuracy,
  COUNT(pa.heading_accuracy) AS num_heading_samples
FROM Player_Attributes pa
GROUP BY
  pa.player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id

params.description: Per-player average heading accuracy and sample count computed from Player_Attributes, at the player (player_api_id, player_fifa_api_id) grain.

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a player dimension or any one-row-per-player view on player_api_id (and player_fifa_api_id when available) — e.g., join to team_identity (if it provides a single row per player) on player_api_id — safe because player_heading_accuracy_agg is one-row-per-player so its measures will not be duplicated. | You may safely left-join this view into match-level or team-level datasets if you immediately re-aggregate after the join (for example, computing team average heading accuracy by taking a weighted or unweighted average grouped by team). Re-aggregation prevents measure duplication from many-to-one joins. | Do NOT directly join this view to a one-to-many child table (for example, Player_Attributes or any match-level table with multiple rows per player) and then sum avg_heading_accuracy or num_heading_samples without re-aggregation — that will multiply/duplicate these measures because the child table introduces additional rows per player. | When joining to sibling aggregated views, ensure the join keys match their grain. For example, joining to a match-aggregate view that is one-row-per-match should be done on match-level keys and followed by appropriate aggregation; do not expect avg_heading_accuracy to remain valid at match grain without recomputation. | If joining on player_fifa_api_id, be cautious: player_fifa_api_id can be null or non-unique in the source. SELECT
  p.player_api_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.player_fifa_api_id,
  p.birthday,
  -- extract year/month/day from birthday text; return NULL when cannot parse
  CASE
    WHEN birthday IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN length(birthday) >= 4 AND substr(birthday,1,4) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' THEN cast(substr(birthday,1,4) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(birthday,'-')>0 THEN
      -- attempt to parse formats like YYYY-M-D or YY-M-D
      CASE
        WHEN cast(substr(birthday,1,instr(birthday,'-')-1) AS INTEGER) >= 100 THEN cast(substr(birthday,1,instr(birthday,'-')-1) AS INTEGER)
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ELSE NULL
  END AS birth_year,
  CASE
    WHEN birthday IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(birthday,'-')>0 THEN
      -- month is the middle component in YYYY-MM-DD or similar
      (CASE
         WHEN length(birthday)>=7 THEN
           cast(substr(birthday, instr(birthday,'-')+1, 2) AS INTEGER)
         ELSE
           NULL
       END)
    WHEN instr(birthday,'/')>0 THEN
      (CASE
         WHEN length(birthday)>=5 THEN
           cast(substr(birthday, instr(birthday,'/')+1, 2) AS INTEGER)
         ELSE NULL
       END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS birth_month,
  CASE
    WHEN birthday IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(birthday,'-')>0 THEN
      (CASE
         WHEN length(birthday)>=10 THEN
           cast(substr(birthday, -2) AS INTEGER)
         ELSE
           NULL
       END)
    WHEN instr(birthday,'/')>0 THEN
      (CASE
         WHEN length(birthday)>=8 THEN
           cast(substr(birthday, -2) AS INTEGER)
         ELSE NULL
       END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS birth_day
FROM players_core p
WHERE birthday IS NOT NULL

Instead, aggregate the player_finishing_attributes measures after joining (or aggregate the underlying Player_Attributes first).   pa.date,
